newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAFEX POSTS RECORD MAIZE TURNOVER IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAFEX POSTS RECORD MAIZE TURNOVER IN JULY.

text.p: The agricultural markets division of the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Friday a record 2,200 contracts worth over 110 million rand had traded on the exchange during July.
It said that some 80,000 tonnes of maize had also been delivered though the exchange due to unstable weather patterns.

"Market players, including maize farmers, maize millers and maize traders are using the futures market to an increasing degree as an effective hedge against adverse price movements in a market subject to the vagaries of nature," Safex said.

It said that white and yellow maize contracts for May 1998 and July 1998 had been listed, which would provide a tool to hedge the possible impact of the expected El Nino weather phenomenon on the maize price.

Global weather experts have become increasingly concerned about the early and intense build-up this year of El Nino, which has in the past been responsible for sparking droughts on one side of the globe while causing floods on the other.
The impact on South Africa is expected to be worst in December, causing drought conditions two months into this country's planting season.
